lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Computers That Help People
lesson.summary: Spot information technology in school, shops and hospitals and say how it helps.
learning_objectives: Name uses of IT beyond school
Make safe, sensible choices with IT

standards.text: Recognise common uses of information technology beyond school
Compare how people live and work before and after the adoption of computing technologies

success_criteria: I can say what IT is
I can name three places that use IT
I can say when to use IT and when to switch off
lesson.real_life: Scanning shopping, crossing at traffic lights and visiting a clinic.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do computers help people?
blocks.say: Today we spot computers that help people. Omar is going shopping with his mum.

blocks.alt: A traffic light showing green with a camera on the pole beside it, against a blue sky
blocks.caption: A traffic light is controlled by a computer.
blocks.credit: Photo by Eliobed Suarez on Unsplash
blocks.say: This traffic light is controlled by a computer. It helps cars and people stay safe.

blocks.text: Stop 1: IT works with a computer

blocks.markdown: **Information technology** means using computers to work with information.
blocks.say: IT stands for information technology. IT means using computers to work with information.

blocks.title: IT is more than a desk computer

scenes.caption: Laptop and tablet.
scenes.say: A laptop is IT. So is a tablet. They help us read and write.

scenes.caption: A cash machine.
scenes.say: A cash machine is IT. It counts money and gives it out.

scenes.caption: Tiny computers inside.
scenes.say: Many machines have a tiny computer inside. They are IT too.

blocks.markdown: A school has **interactive** screens and tablets.
blocks.say: School uses IT too. A smartboard shows lessons. Tablets help us learn.

scenes.caption: Smartboard.
scenes.say: The teacher uses a smartboard. It shows pictures and videos.

scenes.caption: Tablets.
scenes.say: Children use tablets to read and draw.

scenes.caption: Records.
scenes.say: The school office uses a computer to keep records.

question.prompt: Which of these is IT at school?
question.explanation: A smartboard is a computer screen.

blocks.title: Omar at the supermarket
blocks.transcript: Omar goes to the supermarket with his mum. The fruit scale shows the weight on a screen. A packet has a barcode. It is a pattern of lines. The scanner reads the barcode and finds the price. Mum pays with a card machine. It is quick. Outside, traffic lights keep the road safe. Omar's cousin's clinic uses a computer for health records. At home, the family switches off screens for dinner.
blocks.caption: Omar follows his mum through a supermarket in Lahore and spots IT.

points: IT is in school, shops and on roads
Many machines have a tiny computer inside
blocks.say: Let us remember. IT means using computers to work with information. It is all around us.

terms.meaning: Using computers to work with information.
Something you can touch or use to make it respond.
A big touch screen used in a class.
Information that is kept and saved.
A machine that follows instructions.

mini_quiz.prompt: IT is only a computer on a desk.

mini_quiz.explanation: An interactive screen responds to you.

options.text: You can use it and it responds

blocks.text: Stop 1: IT in shops and barcodes

blocks.markdown: A **barcode** is a pattern of lines that holds a number.
blocks.say: In the supermarket, Omar spots a scanner. It reads a barcode on a packet.

scenes.caption: A barcode.
scenes.say: A packet of biscuits has a barcode on the back.

scenes.caption: Scan.
scenes.say: The scanner reads the lines. It finds the price.

scenes.caption: Price.
scenes.say: The checkout shows the price and adds it to the bill.

blocks.title: Scan the shopping
blocks.goal: Move the 5 items past the scanner one at a time.

question.prompt: What does a barcode scanner read?
question.explanation: A scanner reads the pattern of lines.

blocks.text: Stop 2: IT on the road and at the doctor

blocks.markdown: **Traffic lights** and hospital computers are IT.
blocks.say: On the road, traffic lights are IT. At the doctor, computers keep health records safe.

blocks.alt: A traffic light at night with red, amber and green lights glowing
blocks.caption: A traffic light at night. A computer controls the colours.
blocks.credit: Photo by Tsvetoslav Hristov on Unsplash
blocks.say: A computer changes the lights from red to green in order. Cars stop and go safely.

scenes.caption: A record.
scenes.say: A hospital receptionist types a patient's name. The record appears.

scenes.caption: A tablet at the clinic.
scenes.say: A doctor can see the record on a tablet and treat people better.

scenes.caption: IT helps everyone.
scenes.say: Traffic lights, shops and clinics all use IT.

blocks.title: IT spotter
instructions: Walk to the shop, school or street with a grown-up.
Find five things that use IT.
Draw them and say how each one helps.
blocks.say: Now you try. Be an IT spotter on your next walk with a grown-up.

question.prompt: Traffic lights are controlled by a computer.
question.explanation: A computer changes the lights in order.

points: Barcodes hold numbers for scanners to read
Clinics use IT to keep records
blocks.say: Let us remember. IT is in shops, roads and clinics.

terms.meaning: A pattern of lines that holds a number.
A machine that reads a barcode.
Lights that tell cars when to stop and go.
Information that is saved.
A person who greets and helps visitors.

mini_quiz.prompt: Where might you see a barcode?

options.text: On a packet in a shop

mini_quiz.prompt: Which uses IT on the road?

blocks.markdown: IT can make jobs **safer**, easier and more accurate.
blocks.say: IT helps in many ways. It can make jobs safer, easier, quicker and more accurate.

scenes.caption: Easier.
scenes.say: A card machine is quick. You do not need to count coins.

scenes.caption: Accurate.
scenes.say: A scanner is accurate. It reads the number the same way each time.

scenes.caption: Safer.
scenes.say: Traffic lights keep us safe at busy roads.

question.prompt: Which is a way IT helps?

blocks.markdown: Play the memory game. Then think about **benefits**.
blocks.say: First a memory game. Then sort the benefits of IT.

question.prompt: Match each IT tool to how it helps.
question.explanation: Each tool helps in a different way.

points: IT can make jobs safer and easier
blocks.say: Let us remember. IT helps in many ways. But it is not always perfect.

terms.meaning: A good thing that something gives you.
Exactly right.
Less likely to cause harm.
Not so hard to do.
A plan for when something stops working.

mini_quiz.prompt: Which is a benefit of IT?

options.text: Jobs can be done more accurately

mini_quiz.hint: It can make things safer too.

mini_quiz.prompt: What should we have if IT stops working?
mini_quiz.explanation: A backup plan helps if IT stops.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Pick IT for a job

blocks.markdown: Use IT when it **helps**. Think about the job first.
blocks.say: Omar helps plan the family day. He picks IT only when it helps.

blocks.markdown: Pick the right tool for the job.
blocks.say: A map app helps find the shop. A calculator helps check the bill. A phone call can say hello.

scenes.caption: IT job.
scenes.say: A map app helps find the shop. That is a job for IT.

scenes.caption: A person's job.
scenes.say: A hug or a smile needs a person. IT cannot do it.

scenes.caption: Pick the best.
scenes.say: Pick the best helper for each job.

blocks.title: My IT choices
instructions: List five jobs in your day.
Mark which ones could use IT to help.
Mark which ones need a person.
blocks.say: A good choice asks: does IT make this job better?

question.prompt: Which job is best done with a calculator?
question.explanation: A calculator is good for adding.

blocks.markdown: Take **breaks** from screens. Ask a grown-up first.
blocks.say: IT is useful, but we need breaks. Eyes get tired. Switch off at meal times and bedtime.

scenes.caption: Meal time.
scenes.say: At meal time, the family switches off phones and talks.

scenes.caption: Bedtime.
scenes.say: At bedtime, screens are off. Eyes and brains can rest.

scenes.caption: Use wisely.
scenes.say: Using IT wisely means knowing when to stop.

question.prompt: It is wise to switch screens off at bedtime.
question.explanation: Screens off at bedtime helps us rest.

points: Switch off for rest and family time
blocks.say: Let us remember. Pick IT when it helps. Switch off when we need a break.

terms.meaning: Makes something easier or better.
Picking one thing instead of another.
In a sensible way.
Rests from a screen.
A tool that adds and subtracts numbers.
Check with a grown-up before using IT.
